home.name: Michael DiPietro
home.news: DiPietro will start Saturday vs. the Blackhawks.

home.name: John Gibson
home.news: Amid team drama, primarily circulating around Dylan Larkin's trade request, the Red Wings have quietly put together a span of impressive hockey, collecting points in seven of their last eight games (5-1-2). Gibson played well in his most recent outing, saving 18 of 19 shots (.947 SV%) in a 4-1 win over the Chicago Blackhawks. That said, the veteran goalie has had an up-and-down season, posting a 3.15 GAA and .874 SV% in nine games (4-4-1).

away.name: Tristan Jarry
away.news: With Devon Levi (undisclosed) still expected to miss some time, the Oilers will continue to lean on Jarry. The 31-year-old Jarry has impressed as Edmonton's de facto starting goalie, highlighted by his most recent outing, when he saved all 24 shots he faced in a 4-0 shutout win over the Calgary Flames. Jarry has a 2.95 GAA and an .889 SV% in six games this season (3-1-2).

home.name: Jacob Fowler
home.news: Fowler stopped all 46 shots that he faced in the Canadiens' shutout win in St. Louis on Tuesday. He was given the night off in Dallas on Thursday, but will be back between the pipes for his fourth start in the last five games on Saturday. Fowler is one of the hottest goalies in the NHL right now, riding a 6-game winning streak while posting a 1.30 GAA and .954 SV%. Fowler and the Canadiens enter Saturday's game as -117 home favourites.

away.name: Anthony Stolarz
away.news: Stolarz allowed two goals on 32 shots in the Maple Leafs' win in Edmonton last Saturday. Sergei Bobrovsky has started the last two games, but Stolarz will make his sixth start of the season in Vancouver. He's played well so far, going 4-1-0 with a 2.79 GAA and .907 SV%, and draws a great matchup as -181 road favourites.

home.name: Jake Oettinger
home.news: Oettinger had a rare rough outing on Thursday, giving up four goals on 20 shots in the Stars' loss to Montreal. He'll have a chance to redeem himself Saturday vs. a Columbus team that has scored just 2.45 goals per game (29th in the NHL). Oettinger has performed much better on the road than in Dallas, where he 4-3-0 with a 2.28 GAA but an .884 SV%.
